name: White supremacy
summary: White supremacy is the belief that white people are inherently superior to other races and should hold power, privilege and often separate territory. Its adherents draw on 19th and early 20th century race science, defend or seek segregation, exclusion of non-white immigrants and denial of equal political rights, and frequently adopt antisemitic conspiracy theories. Strands range from legal segregationists and slaveholder ideology to Nazi-style racial states, white nationalist ethnostate projects and violent militias.
scope: The mainstream of explicitly white-supremacist belief as documented in Wikipedia's account of the doctrine, with Madison Grant's The Passing of the Great Race and Alexander Stephens's Cornerstone Speech as primary expressions, plus white nationalist separatism. It does not cover the broader topic of racism or non-white supremacist movements, and economic and religious positions vary widely between strands.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Welfare provision is generally framed around the in-group and not a stated concern of the sources, so an adherent would likely oppose broad state benefits that also serve non-whites; inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Economic policy is secondary to race in the sources; wage floors are inferred to be opposed as part of the usual far-right economic outlook.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Strands split between market-friendly and anti-capitalist positions, as the sources centre on racial control of resources, not on markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Neo-Nazi strands favour state economic control while others favour private enterprise; the sources document no common line.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Some strands attack Jewish finance while others defend white property-holders; economic questions are not settled in the sources.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are not a topic of the sources; adherents are inferred to oppose them as multiracial or leftist bodies.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property was central to slaveholder defences of racial order, but modern strands are split on property rights; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The sources do not address regulation; strands split between anti-corporate and pro-business views.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare is commonly framed as benefiting non-white groups, so many adherents favour cutting it; inferred, as the sources say little.

worker-ownership.rationale: No source supports collective ownership; it is inferred to be rejected as a left-wing programme.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Anti-government militias and distrust of the state suggest opposition to surveillance, though the sources do not state it.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the generally conservative and authoritarian social outlook of the movement.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents routinely oppose laws that would restrict racist speech; inferred from their position as its main targets.

strong-leader.rationale: Grant favoured rule by a picked minority and Nazism exalted a leader; inferred as the typical authoritarian lean.

state-harmful.rationale: Historic supremacists wanted the state to enforce racial hierarchy, though militias are hostile to government; most adherents are not anarchists.

limit-guns.rationale: Militia and armed-group culture in the movement suggests opposition to gun limits; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Segregationist states relied on police power while modern militias distrust the federal government, so strands split.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the rigid views on sexuality noted in the sources.

decide-locally.rationale: Segregation was defended via states' rights, but nationalist strands want central white-majority states; split.

rehabilitation.rationale: Grant's eugenics stresses inherited traits and removing defective lines over reform; inferred opposition.

traditional-family.rationale: Sources note rigid views on gender and sexuality in some groups and concern for white birth rates.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The sources note that white supremacist groups target LGBTQ+ people.

abortion-legal.rationale: Concern for white birth rates and Grant's pro-natal aims for desired groups point to opposition; inferred and not uniform.

more-religion-public.rationale: Christian Identity favours religious politics while Creativity is atheist and others are pagan; genuinely split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The doctrine rejects racial equality as a principle, so adherents reject redress for racial injustice.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the rigid view of sex and gender roles in some groups.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: White nationalists see white culture as foremost and Grant sought to preserve Nordic heritage.

gradual-change.rationale: Violent and revolutionary strands seek radical restructuring and Grant despaired of existing institutions; inferred.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration restriction is central: Grant, the 1790 and 1920s laws and white nationalist aims all stress it.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Conspiracy theories about global Jewish control and nationalism imply hostility to international bodies; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Nationalist economics is inferred; the sources do not address trade.

nation-first.rationale: Nationalist strands prioritise their own nation, though loyalty is to race across borders; inferred.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred from hostility to universalist human rights claims and non-white beneficiaries.

open-borders.rationale: Open borders contradict the central aim of preserving a white majority or homeland.

limit-growth.rationale: Grant was interested in conservation but strands disagree on growth; not a defining issue.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The sources do not address climate; inferred from the movement's general hostility to expert-led state action.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; strands diverge on modernity.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; no common line among strands.

revolution-justified.rationale: Militia groups seek to overthrow the government and form a white homeland, though mainstream segregationists worked through the law.

experts-over-public.rationale: Grant held that a majority is inferior to a picked minority, though modern movements distrust expert elites; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred opposition to socialist planning, though Nazism used heavy state direction.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred as a left-wing economic model the movement rejects.

land-value-tax.rationale: None of the sources address this issue, and strands of the movement differ; left neutral.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Grant favoured hereditary advantage and lines of good stock; inferred opposition to heavy inheritance taxes.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred from opposition to unconditional benefits that also reach non-whites.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic nationalism is a common lean; the sources do not state it.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Strands split between statist and market positions.

widespread-small-property.rationale: None of the sources address this issue, and strands of the movement differ; left neutral.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: No source supports abolishing money; it is a left-wing aim the movement rejects.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Creativity and other groups promote conspiracies about Jewish control of banks, suggesting hostility to central banking; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Nazi-influenced strands favoured it while others did not address it.

one-party-rule.rationale: Nazism and one-party Jim Crow South relied on it but other strands are indifferent.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Grant admired aristocracy, but strands lack a common view on monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Non-whites were disenfranchised and Grant argued universal suffrage favours the average over the capable.

workers-councils.rationale: A left-wing form of rule the movement rejects.

right-to-secede.rationale: The Confederacy and modern white-homeland aims depend on secession; inferred as a general attitude.

natural-rulers.rationale: Racial superiority and Grant's rule by the picked best are core to the doctrine.

political-violence-never.rationale: Lynchings, the Holocaust and attacks like Christchurch show the movement's acceptance of violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Grant called war dysgenic while Nazism glorified it; strands split.

separate-church-state.rationale: Strands span Christian Identity, paganism and atheism.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Christian Identity favours it but others do not.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred as a libertarian idea at odds with state enforcement of racial order.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from Nazism, colonial dominance and the focus on racial power.

ethnic-nation.rationale: A mainly white nation or white ethnostate is the central nationalist aim.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The doctrine puts race, not class, as the driver of history, as with Stoddard's racial struggle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Grant and Stephens deny natural equality.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: White supremacy justified colonialism and dispossession, such as in Native Land Court practice.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Colonialism was justified by white supremacy, so owing reparations is rejected; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-white unity across nations appears in Nordic and Aryan racial doctrines.

self-interest-moral.rationale: None of the sources address this issue, and strands of the movement differ; left neutral.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Inferred from collectivist racial duty in Nazi-influenced strands.

limit-population.rationale: Concern for low white birth rates points against limiting population generally, though Grant wanted undesirable lines reduced.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Mainstream strands credit white civilisation with achievement; esoteric strands oppose modernity.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred from traditionalist and restorationist outlook.

human-enhancement.rationale: Eugenic strands favour breeding for improvement, but this concerns technology; split.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: None of the sources address this issue, and strands of the movement differ; left neutral.

restore-past-order.rationale: Adherents lament decline of a white order, as with Grant.

direct-action.rationale: Violent militias and street groups favour direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: None of the sources address this issue, and strands of the movement differ; left neutral.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Rejected as contrary to claims of white civilisational achievement.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Marxist claim the movement rejects.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: A Marxist doctrine the movement rejects.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist analysis rejected; some strands blame Jewish finance for wars.

taxation-theft.rationale: Split between libertarian-leaning and statist strands.

harm-principle.rationale: Grant would restrict individuals for racial ends; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The doctrine ascribes standing to racial groups and denies equal rights.

conscription.rationale: None of the sources address this issue, and strands of the movement differ; left neutral.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred from stress on racial homeland and membership.

positive-liberty.rationale: Inferred as rejected egalitarian welfare liberalism.

media-academia-power.rationale: Creativity promotes a theory of Jewish control of governments, banks and media.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Innate racial differences in ability are the core claim.

organic-representation.rationale: None of the sources address this issue, and strands of the movement differ; left neutral.

total-state.rationale: Nazi strands favoured it; others did not.

national-rebirth.rationale: Grant ends with FINIS AMERICAE and decline-and-renewal rhetoric is common.

territorial-expansion.rationale: White supremacy justified European colonialism and Nazi expansion.

bound-labor.rationale: Slavery was defended but bound agricultural labour of this form is not documented as a position.

universal-morality.rationale: None of the sources address this issue, and strands of the movement differ; left neutral.

single-common-good.rationale: None of the sources address this issue, and strands of the movement differ; left neutral.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Views on Israel are split; many oppose Zionism, others support Israel.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: None of the sources address this issue, and strands of the movement differ; left neutral.

revive-national-language.rationale: None of the sources address this issue, and strands of the movement differ; left neutral.

school-vouchers.rationale: None of the sources address this issue, and strands of the movement differ; left neutral.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: None of the sources address this issue, and strands of the movement differ; left neutral.

economic-freedom.rationale: None of the sources address this issue, and strands of the movement differ; left neutral.

rule-by-example.rationale: Grant favoured rule by the wisest and best, but nothing on moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: A white homeland and nationhood is central to nationalist strands.

force-without-un.rationale: Nationalist and militarist strands do not defer to international bodies; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Creativity is atheist while Christian Identity is faith-based.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from the focus on excluding non-whites.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from opposition to welfare dependency.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nazi-influenced racial community ideas stress cooperation.

workers-nation.rationale: National racial community stressed over class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The sources note rigid gender views in some groups.

ban-interest.rationale: Some strands attack Jewish finance but this is not stated as a ban.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Segregation, apartheid and racial classification by law are core.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist theory the movement rejects.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: None of the sources address this issue, and strands of the movement differ; left neutral.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Non-white immigration is opposed outright, not accepted subject to assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: Great Replacement or white genocide beliefs are widely held among adherents.

proportional-representation.rationale: None of the sources address this issue, and strands of the movement differ; left neutral.

national-mission.rationale: None of the sources address this issue, and strands of the movement differ; left neutral.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Conspiracy theories about elites, such as ZOG, are widespread.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Grant argues the state through sterilization must stop defective lines.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from sympathy for state violence against non-whites.

night-watchman-state.rationale: None of the sources address this issue, and strands of the movement differ; left neutral.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Marriage outside the white race is rejected and Grant calls race crossing reversion to the lower type.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Cornerstone Speech rests the Confederacy on the principle that the races are not equal, and the doctrine denies equal rights before the law.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Economic doctrine varies widely between strands and the issue is outside the sources; inferred.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Adherents defend white settler states and colonial rule as the proper outcome of white superiority.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Adherents want rights and law to differ by race, and many want a Christian-identified order, so they would not favour religion-blind uniform law; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Strands differ on religion and the sources do not address conversion; inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not an issue in the sources; adherents are indifferent.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religion is split between strands (Christian Identity, pagan, secular) and the sources do not address schooling; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The premise is a socialist state, which the doctrine does not address; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Adherents limit political participation to whites, as in the Cornerstone Speech, so authority rests on the consent of a restricted group only; inferred.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Adherents rely on race science as objective truth, though some claim establishment knowledge is biased against them; inferred.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade policy is not a defining concern and strands differ; no source states a position.

population-transfer.rationale: White nationalist projects seek an ethnostate and exclusion or removal of non-white populations.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Segregation, subordination and violence against non-whites are central to the doctrine, so force is not restricted to defence.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Grant presents racial struggle and survival of the fittest race as the driver of history.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Adherents would back banning opposing movements but not their own; the sources give no clear position, so this leans on inference.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Stephens and Grant accept subordination of a racial group as the legitimate basis of social order; inferred for domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Grant favours elite racial rule and sceptical views of democracy; inferred rather than stated on division of power.

vanguard-party.rationale: The doctrine is not framed around the working class or revolutionary parties; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Grant's eugenics and elite rule treat the unfit as a burden, and welfare is framed around the in-group; inferred.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Inferred: public housing is not addressed, and strands range from welfare-minded to free-market.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred: the audit finds a lean against unions, so limits on strikes fit, though this is not a stated concern.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Inferred: the sources blame race, not population growth, and economic views vary by strand.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Grant treats race mixture as a reversion to the lower type, and white nationalists want racially homogeneous states.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Stephens and Grant rest government on racial hierarchy and elite rule, which a lottery among all citizens would undo.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred: authoritarian strands accept suspending protections against perceived enemies, while others emphasize constitutional rights.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address price controls and economic positions vary widely between strands.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred: Nazi-style strands favor state control of information, while other strands rely on free speech claims.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred: Nazi-style strands put the army under the party, but segregationist and militia strands do not.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from its support for immigration limits: a long wait fits, though many adherents would deny non-white citizenship entirely.

missingStatements.text: Marriage and having children across racial lines should be discouraged.
missingStatements.rationale: Marriage outside the white race is usually rejected and Grant calls race crossing reversion to the lower type.

notes: Economic positions (market versus statist) and religion (Christian Identity, paganism, atheism) vary sharply between strands, so many answers on those topics are low confidence or neutral. Many answers rest on inference because the sources focus on race and not on policy.
